source.title: Encapsulation of primary dopaminergic neurons in a GDNF-loaded collagen hydrogel increases their survival, re-innervation and function after intra-striatal transplantation

material: Type 1 collagen hydrogel cross-linked with 4 mg/ml 4s-StarPEG (no GDNF), encapsulating E14 VM cells

biology.cell_type: E14 rat ventral mesencephalon dopaminergic neurons

other_outcomes.evidence: The optimised collagen hydrogel successfully formed in situ after intra-striatal delivery and was still present 14 days post-transplantation (Fig. 4B).
other_outcomes.name: in vivo hydrogel persistence

notes: Densities 200,000-400,000 cells; no significant effect on TH+ survival or re-innervation at 14 days; reduced microgliosis and astrocytosis.
